summary_rationale: DLF combines an elite, net-cash balance sheet (₹15,084 Cr cash vs ₹314 Cr borrowings as of Sep 2026, though ₹12,270 Cr is RERA-escrowed), a 188 msf legacy land bank, and a 50 msf AAA-rated annuity platform (DCCDL at 96% occupancy) that cushions housing cycles. However, its development business remains inherently cyclical and lumpy—72% of land potential and 84% of recent sales are concentrated in Gurugram/NCR, H1FY27 pre-sales fell 72% YoY to ₹4,460 Cr against ₹20,000 Cr full-year guidance, reported ROCE (6.3%) and ROE (9.6%) are modest due to Ind AS 115 revenue lag and idle land/cash, and P&L earnings include material Other Income and JV valuation gains.
